editorial:
You follow Mickey Barnes, an ordinary guy who takes a job where dying is part of the workday. On a harsh new world, he is printed again after every fatal mistake, and each new version remembers the last. When a mix-up leaves two Mickeys alive at once, the story turns into a funny, tense, and surprisingly heartfelt sci-fi adventure about identity, survival, and standing up to a boss who treats people like tools.

Robert Pattinson makes the two Mickeys feel different without overdoing it, and the movie balances big laughs with sharp satire. The world looks great, the pacing stays lively, and the side characters add plenty of chaos. It can get a little messy in the middle, and some jokes land harder than others, but the energy rarely drops. If you like weird sci-fi with heart, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, the two Mickeys team up to stop Marshall from wiping out the native creepers. Their plan works, but the duplicate problem is solved when one Mickey dies and the other keeps going with their shared memories. With Marshall out of power, the colony gets a second chance, and Mickey finally gets to live as just one person instead of a replaceable worker.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird sci-fi adventures with humor and heart.
